title: Remote Wi-Fi messaging: MQTT, TLS, and cloud connections

spans.text: A device on a local network is not automatically reachable from the internet. This lesson shows how a sensor can publish to a cloud broker and protect that connection.

In STA mode the device joins a router; if that router has internet, the device can connect to a remote MQTT broker over TLS. MQTT is publish/subscribe messaging: a device publishes a reading to a topic and an app subscribes. QoS describes delivery guarantees, retained messages keep the latest value, and Last Will can report an unexpected disconnect. A local HTTP server can work without internet. For remote access, prefer authenticated encrypted services and narrowly scoped topics over exposing a device port. NAT and firewalls usually prevent direct inbound connections to a device behind a home router.

with a TLS broker on port 8883. Connect Wi-Fi in STA mode first; use a CA certificate and broker account that you control.

spans.title: Important safety and compatibility note
spans.text: `PubSubClient` is a separate dependency, and Wi-Fi must already be connected. This sketch publishes a fixed `23.5`; read a real sensor, check the connection result, and never commit passwords or tokens.
